hook: Ocean currents alone predict where coastal populations share ancestry, beating the standard distance model.
summary: A simulation of larvae drifting on ocean currents predicts broad regions of similar genetic makeup, each set by the nearest upstream source population, with sharp breaks between regions. Genomic data from a salt marsh mussel along the coast matched these predictions well. The test is on one species, so how widely the framework holds is still open.
title: Ocean current models predict spatial structure for coastal biodiversity
